newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: FISCHER CHALLENGES LABOR ON COLSTON
Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer says the Labor Party seems determined to use Independent Senator Mal Colston's vote at every stage, in a grubby exercise.
Mr Fischer has challenged the Opposition to follow the Government's lead and refuse to accept the vote of Senator Colston, while the Federal Police investigate alleged travel rorts.
Meanwhile, Senator Colston has gone to ground following his discharge yesterday from a Brisbane hospital.
Senate President Margaret Reid is still waiting for him to return her call of earlier this week, to discuss his future as Deputy President.
TELSTRA TO PAY COMMONWEALTH THREE-BILLION DOLLARS
Rating agency Standard and Poor's has lowered its long-term credit rating for Telstra following its announcement that it'll pay three-billion dollars to the Commonwealth before privatisation.
Telstra says it'll borrow money to finance the payout, which is aimed to help reduce the government's budget deficit.
The payment is expected to be completed by the end of the financial year.
Telstra's long-term credit rating has been lowered from triple-A, to Double-A-plus the rating outlook has been revised down from stable, to negative.
Communications Minister Richard Alston says Telstra's current debt levels are low by international standards.
"MAD DOG" PAROLE HEARING UNDERWAY
A parole hearing has just got underway in Sydney into whether Archie 'Mad Dog' McCafferty should be released from a New South Wales prison.
McCafferty was given a life sentence in 1973 for the murder of three people in Sydney's west.
Relatives of the victims are attending the New South Wales parole board hearing along with a large media contingent.
While Australian Immigration Authorities are planning to deport McCafferty on his release, a British Labor MP has called for him to stay in Australia.
QUEENSLAND PRISONS BOSS LIKELY TO BE STOOD DOWN

The Queensland Corrective Services Commission Director General, Keith Hamburger, has been asked to take leave and will probably be stood down after the release of a report on the Woodford Prison riot.
Minister Russell Cooper says he has had preliminary talks with the Premier about a suitable role which will use Mr Hamburger's skills.
QCSC chairman Trevor Carlyon says Mr Hamburger will be on leave for about two weeks until the board can make a final decision after it receives detailed response to the inspectors report.
The report has also identified the transfer of unsuitable prisoners to Woodford as one of the key reasons to the riot.
WHEAT BOARD ABOLISHED
The President of the Grains Council of Australia, Jeff Arney, has welcomed the replacement of the Australian Wheat Board with a private grower-controlled and owned company.
Federal Primary Industries Minister, John Anderson, says the new structure will be in place by July, and will be responsible for all commercial aspects of wheat marketing.
The Wheat Industry Fund, to which growers have contributed since 1989, is to be converted into shares to provide capital backing for the new company.
Mr Arney says the new structure is a positive business step for the nation's four-billion dollar wheat industry.
SPORTS NEWS
News Limited's director of sport, Ian Frykberg says he thinks the chances are good for a negotiated settlement this year with the ARL.
Mr Frykberg says he expects to see one competition,with a rationalisation in the number of teams in Sydney starting in 1998.
Tonight in league, Balmain faces North Sydney and the Hunter Mariners are at home to Perth.
High winds have been forecast for Invercargill this afternoon for the Brumbies Super 12 game against Otago.
Captain Brett Robinson and centre James Holbeck have been cleared to play.
Australia leads the medal table after the opening day of the World Shortcourse swimming titles in Sweden.
Emma Johnson and Mathew Dunn won the 400 medley while the 4 by 100 medley relay team of Radley, Klim, Huegull and Rogers broke the world record.
Hawthorn has lost John Platten for tomorow nights AFL game against the West Coast Eagles.
Geelong has been strengthened by the return of
Brownless..Pickering...and McGrath for Sunday's game against Essendon.
Tonight Melbourne faces the Western Bulldogs at the MCG.
British bookmakers Ladbrokes have accepted a bet at 50 to 1 from a punter who believes Tiger Woods will be elected President of the United States by the time he reaches 50 years of age.
And it's a big day in tennis for Australia at Japan Open.
Todd Woodbridge takes on Pat Rafter in one quarter final with Mark Woodforde playing Thomas Johannson in another.
While Annabell Ellwood faces Amy Frazier in the womens singles.
